target: leaflet amount up to 12 (6 pairs); or count 6 of leaflet pairs
fix: 'n-jugate' counts pairs of leaflets, not leaflets: read 'to 6-jugate' as up to 6 pairs (up to 12 lateral leaflets). Do not use the number as a leaflet count.
reason: The leaves are up to 6-jugate, meaning up to 6 pairs of leaflets. The annotation turns this into at most 6 leaflets.
The spikelets are ± loosely arranged in the spike. 'loose' with the approximately qualifier says this.

fix: Read 'almost X' as approximately X. Do not drop the hedge, or the statement becomes stronger than the flora's.
reason: The flora says the subshrubs are only 'almost matlike'. Saying plainly that they form mats goes beyond the text.
'petals ... adaxially pubescent' means the adaxial surface of the petal is pubescent.
In FNA Eriogonum, 'Herbs ... H × W dm' gives height × width, so height is 20–35(–45) cm.
The flora says the leaves are sessile.

fix: Keep the sex word ('female', 'pistillate', 'male', 'staminate') before a part as context. Without it the statement is wrong for the other sex.
reason: Only the female inflorescence is short. The male spikes are 3–6 cm, so 'inflorescence short' is false without 'female'.
In height × width, the second range (3–8 dm) is the plant's width: 30–80 cm.
In FNA, a single size with no 'diam.' is the length: fruits 17–20 mm.
In 'Leaves 10–46 cm × 1.5–4 mm', the second range is the blade width.
The statement is in the Bark section: 'Smooth'.
The flora gives seed length as 0.8–1 cm.
The female spikes are many-flowered: many flowers inside the inflorescence.
The capsules reach past the floral tube (the hypanthium), so they are longer than it.
'Seta single' means one seta.

target: glabrescent on the adaxial leaflet surface (position 'above')
fix: In 'X on both sides or Y above', give each alternative its own place. Y applies only to the upper (adaxial) surface.
reason: The leaflets are pilose on both sides, or glabrate only above. The annotation gives glabrescent as an alternative for the whole leaflet.
Young branches are pubescent and later become glabrescent. Glabrescent with the 'mature' context is right.
The flora says the perianth segments (tepals) are ovate.
The bracteal cups are often numerous in clusters. Counting them as many bracts is acceptable, though 'often' is not recorded.
The flora says stamens 6.
'blades ... apex trigonous' means the tip of the leaf blade is three-sided.
The width is 0.5–3(–5) dm, which is 5–30(–50) cm.

target: staminal column apex teeth (not a leaf-blade tooth; the part is the staminal column / fused filaments)
fix: When 'with n apical teeth' follows a non-leaf part (staminal column, calyx tube), the teeth belong to that part. Do not map them to a leaf-blade tooth.
reason: The 5 apical teeth are on the staminal column. They are not teeth of a leaf blade inside a stamen.
The flora says the sexual condition is paroicous or autoicous.
The capitula sit in a corymb-like compound inflorescence.
'without thickened roots' is a negated thick root.

target: pistillate pedicel, length 2.8–3.4 mm in fruit
fix: In 'Pedicels: staminate X; pistillate Y', each measurement belongs to the pedicel of that sex. Keep the sex.
reason: The 2.8–3.4 mm is for pistillate pedicels only. Staminate pedicels are 1.5–1.9 mm.

fix: In 'colour-ish + hair word' (brownish puberulent, rusty tomentose), the colour belongs to the hairs, not the part.
reason: 'brownish puberulent' describes the colour of the hairs. It says nothing about the colour of the peduncle.
The twig hairs are soon shed. At maturity the twigs are tan and glabrous, and glabrous with the 'mature' context matches.

fix: 'glaucous' means covered with a waxy bloom (PATO_0104277). Do not map it to green.
reason: The fruit is slightly glaucous, meaning it has a bloom. It is not green.
